name: Cobalt Grid
summary: A two-colour trend report from a lab notebook: cream paper, electric cobalt as the ONLY ink, a permanent graph-paper grid, Newsreader serif, data drawn as grid cells, a stair-stepped pixel-glitch band and data patches; everything prints on in hard steps, never fades.

palette.use: ink: ALL type, rules, grid, glitch, data patches, data cells
ink-soft: editorial subtitles only (the italic callout)
ink at 18% on paper: faint row dividers (proposed flat hex)
the same ink: there's no second colour

type.case: sentence case Newsreader; uppercase micro labels and mono chrome
type.emphasis: size, a face switch (Hanken to Newsreader), a mono delta arrow or opacity; never a hue, never bold

banned: a second ink colour; bold Newsreader; rounded corners; circles; drop shadows
disabling the grid or the hairlines
crowding chapter, quote or closing frames; edge-to-edge headlines
fades, blurs and soft easing on anything: it prints in hard steps
gradients other than the scanline bars; halftones and translucent overprints (that's another medium)
a real, scannable code: data patches are texture
